definition: Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers, an LLM by Google.
details: Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers, an LLM by Google.

explainer.lead: BART is a Google language model whose name describes two key ingredients: reading input bidirectionally and writing output auto-regressively. This lets it use context from both sides of the input while producing text in order.

tiers.eli5: Imagine reading a whole sentence before answering a question about it, so every word can help you understand the others. Then imagine writing your answer one word at a time, with each new word depending on what you have already written. BART combines those two ways of working with language.
tiers.practitioner: An implementation separates a bidirectional encoding pass over the input from an auto-regressive decoding loop over the output. Each decoding step conditions on the encoded input and the tokens generated so far. A common pitfall is treating BART as only an encoder or only a decoder, rather than a combination of both.
tiers.paperLevel: For input x = (x_1, ..., x_n), let H = Enc(x) denote bidirectional contextual representations. The output distribution factorizes as p(y | x) = product_t p(y_t | y_<t, H). Auto-regressive decoding is inherently sequential and cannot condition on future output tokens.

explainer.example: Given “The cat sat on the mat,” the bidirectional encoder can use the whole sentence when representing “cat.” The decoder might then generate “A cat is sitting” from left to right, with each token conditioned on the tokens already produced.

components.name: Input sequence: the text to be processed.
Bidirectional encoder: builds input representations using context from both directions.
Auto-regressive decoder: generates output tokens in sequence.
Generated sequence: the text produced by the decoder.

flow: Encode the input with bidirectional context.
Predict the next output token from the encoded input and previous output tokens.
Append that token and repeat until generation ends.
explainer.origin: BART, short for Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers, is a large language model developed by Google.
explainer.lineage: Its name identifies its Transformer-based lineage and its combination of bidirectional input representations with auto-regressive output generation.
explainer.whyItMatters: BART brings whole-input context and ordered text generation into one model, connecting language understanding with language generation.

nodes.label: Auto-regressive decoder
nodes.note: Predicts one output token at a time.

diagram.caption: BART encodes the complete input bidirectionally, then generates output auto-regressively.
